A1.justification: Both PDFs describe OSVI-WM and contain readable main text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices. Existing material can be matched reliably across pagination and appendix reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original simulation and real-world success rates, component ablations, and qualitative robot rollouts in Section 4 and the appendix.

after.justification: v2 retains these original results and adds Meta-World training-task exclusion experiments in Section 4.2.

M1.justification: The encoder, recursive action/world models, waypoint prediction, training losses, and replanning procedure are unchanged. Section 3.2 clarifies that real-world replanning was not used, consistent with v1 Section 4.1. Suggested completion detectors are future options, not implemented components.

E1.justification: Both versions use Meta-World, Pick-and-Place, Two-Franka-PP, Human-Franka-PP, and Human-Franka-Push. The revised split and task-exclusion ablations operate within existing task coverage; no new domain, embodiment, or test-task requirement is introduced.

E2.justification: Tables 1–2 retain the same comparator membership: DAML, T-OSVI, AWDA with and without additional data, and T-OSVI* in their respective experiments. Newly discussed DINOBot and Gr00t are not added as reported benchmark comparisons.

E3.justification: Sections 4.1 and A3.2 revise Pick-and-Place from 15 training/1 test task to 14 training/2 test tasks, without establishing whether results were rerun. Section 4.2 adds training-set exclusion controls for Button-Press and Window-Open. Appendix A4.3's replanning budgets newly document the existing Figure 8 experiment.

E4.justification: Section 4.2 adds two sensitivity tests probing dependence on related training tasks: excluding button-related tasks and excluding Window-Close. Appendix A4.3 adds a time-cost analysis of existing replanning results. Previous architectural ablations, visualizations, and failure cases remain.

E5.justification: Neither version reports training-seed variability, confidence intervals, or significance tests. Existing evaluation counts of 100 simulation rollouts per task and 25 real-world rollouts are retained; the added results also use point estimates.

E6.justification: Numbers in Tables 1–3 and existing plots are retained. New task-exclusion results report 97% Button-Press success and 80% Window-Open success versus 95% with Window-Close training data. Appendix A4.3 adds episode timings of 40 seconds without replanning and 160 seconds with replanning. These are additional findings, not improved headline scores.

T1.justification: The problem formulation, latent-state/action equations, loss definitions, and appendix explanation of Soft-DTW are unchanged. Added dynamics and generalization explanations introduce no formal assumptions, derivations, theorems, or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introductory contributions, and main conclusion retain the same claims about world-model-guided one-shot imitation, unseen-task generalization, and comparative performance. Added evidence and limitations do not redefine the central contribution.

C2.justification: v2 explains the world-model loss as a dynamics-consistency regularizer and interprets task-exclusion results through transferable skills and task complexity. It adds limitations concerning train/test division and the same family of manipulators, plus discussion of replanning overhead and world models versus VLAs.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code-availability link, RealSense D455/D435 camera identities, 640×480 capture resolution and calibration information in A3.3, and 500-step versus 2000-step execution budgets with timings in A4.3. These expand documentation rather than establish hardware or implementation changes.

R1.justification: Four references are added: DINOBot, Gr00t N1, RoboDexVLM, and Autonomous Interactive Correction MLLM. Related discussion distinguishes external-camera imitation from egocentric approaches and adds VLA positioning and possible completion detectors. Existing cited works are retained.

P1.justification: There are localized prose expansions and clarifications. Appendix A4 becomes Additional Comparisons, with existing visualization discussion grouped under A4.1 and new A4.2–A4.3 subsections. An acknowledgements section is added; the overall narrative and method exposition remain largely intact.

P2.justification: All three tables, nine main figures, and eleven appendix figures are retained with unchanged display content and designs. Text reflow changes figure positioning and moves Table 3 lower on page 9; appendix figures follow the inserted discussion on later pages.

improvement.justification: The task-exclusion ablations and explicit generalization limits make the unseen-task claims better supported and more carefully bounded. Replanning costs, camera details, and the code link improve transparency. The gain is limited: headline results remain numerically unchanged, and the unexplained Pick-and-Place split revision leaves uncertainty about whether its scores were recomputed.
